title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote:
An Empirical Study of Retrieval-enhanced
Graph Neural Networks

extractions.description: The paper explores the effectiveness of retrieval-enhanced Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) by introducing GRAPH RETRIEVAL, a scheme that retrieves similar graphs to augment information learned by GNNs. It demonstrates substantial improvements over existing GNNs on various datasets, especially for datasets with long-tailed label distributions.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper does not focus on sustainable development as a central theme.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on improving the performance of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) using a retrieval-enhanced approach. While GNNs can be applied to various domains, including those related to climate change and sustainability, this paper does not directly address or focus on these areas. The primary focus is on the methodology for enhancing GNN performance.
primary_category.quote: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are effective tools for graph representation learning. ... we want to explore how the re- trieval idea can help augment the useful information learned in the graph neural networks

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper's focus is on improving GNN performance generally, rather than targeting a specific Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: Motivated by the success of retrieval-enhanced models in language and vision domains [22, 11, 29], in this paper, we aim at exploring the effects of retrieval-enhancement in the regime of GNNs.

new_primary_category.justification: There is no need for a new primary category.
